stem.text: Consider the differential equation \( \frac{dy}{dx} = 6 x^{2} - 2 y - 2 \). Without drawing it, describe the field of slope segments for this equation: where the segments are horizontal, where they have positive slope, and where they have negative slope.

answer_key.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the parabola \( y = 3 x^{2} - 1 \), have positive slope where \( y < 3 x^{2} - 1 \), and have negative slope where \( y > 3 x^{2} - 1 \).

worked_solution.text: A segment is horizontal where the right side is 0: \( 6 x^{2} - 2 y - 2 = 0 \) exactly when \( y = 3 x^{2} - 1 \), which is the parabola \( y = 3 x^{2} - 1 \).
The right side equals \( -2\left(- 3 x^{2} + y + 1\right) \), so its sign is positive where \( y < 3 x^{2} - 1 \) and negative where \( y > 3 x^{2} - 1 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the slope on each side of the locus

options.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the line \( y = -1 \), have positive slope where \( y < -1 \), and have negative slope where \( y > -1 \).
options.derivation: the slope read as depending on y alone, the x term ignored, so the segments would match along horizontal lines

options.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the parabola \( y = 3 x^{2} - 1 \), have positive slope where \( y < 3 x^{2} - 1 \), and have negative slope where \( y > 3 x^{2} - 1 \).
The segments are horizontal exactly along the parabola \( x = 3 y^{2} - 1 \), have positive slope where \( x < 3 y^{2} - 1 \), and have negative slope where \( x > 3 y^{2} - 1 \).
options.derivation: each lattice point read with its coordinates exchanged, so x and y trade places

options.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the parabola \( y = 3 x^{2} - 1 \), have positive slope where \( y > 3 x^{2} - 1 \), and have negative slope where \( y < 3 x^{2} - 1 \).
options.derivation: the horizontal row located but the tilt on each side taken from the look of a familiar field instead of from a computed slope
